intro: Muriel Nguyen Xuan plays Chopin’s Waltz in D♭ major, Op. 64 No. 1, the Minute Waltz, on a Yamaha grand, in a recording made by Stéphane Magnenat in 2007. Between the fast outer sections, a melody marked sostenuto runs over the same three-beat bass.

sections.label: A · right-hand circling figure
sections.mNote: The bass enters after four unaccompanied bars.

sections.label: B · Sostenuto melody in longer notes
sections.mNote: Sostenuto melody above the left hand’s three beats.

sections.label: A′ · Trills, return of quaver theme
sections.mNote: The left hand rests before the running figure returns.

sections.label: Coda · Descending scale to D♭
sections.mNote: A long descending scale ends on the final D♭.

cues.title: Opening, bars 1–12
cues.text: Molto vivace, very lively; leggiero, lightly. Chopin begins with quavers turning around A♭. The left hand rests for four bars, then plays a bass note and two chords in each bar, and the right hand soon rises into a tune.
cues.evidence: Peters edition, bars 1–12, including the opening markings. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=483
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Nguyen Xuan and Magnenat recording, 2007
cues.text: Nguyen Xuan played a Yamaha grand, and Magnenat recorded her with two AKG microphones and Audacity running on Linux. The recording dates from their collaboration in 2007. They released it under both their names with a licence that allows free sharing.
cues.evidence: The original recording’s embedded description lists the piano, microphones and software; the licence names both collaborators. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Muriel-Nguyen-Xuan-Chopin-valse-opus64-1.ogg

cues.title: Final descent and cadence
cues.text: The right hand leaps up an octave, then runs down through a group of twenty-four notes. For most of the descent the left hand does not play. The waltz ends on a D♭ in the right hand over a bass chord, closing in D♭ major.
cues.evidence: Peters edition, bars 121–125: octave displacement and the descending group marked 24, followed by the final D♭ major cadence. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=483

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: Composer for the piano, known for music that drew on operatic singing and on the irregular accents of the mazurka.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832 Chopin, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist, played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. He had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers, and teaching soon supplied his living. For the rest of his life his profession depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from one concert city to the next; Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. The family moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
